sections.title: Todo App
sections.body: In todo app I got to build a small todo app with javascript!

sections.heading: Remarks
paragraphs: So this was the first 'serious' so to speak exercise using Javascript. The main focus of this exercise was to explore encapsulation, a programming approach where data and methods are bundled into objects/classes. This way you protect the scope of variables and methods and avoid accidents like rendering defunct key parts of your app's inner workings.

Some of the encapsulating methods explored were: using an object, a constructor function as well as classes. While classes are supposedly all the jazz and the ones preferred for encapsulation I personally preferred the syntax of constructor functions. Just because one language follows the class approach doesn't mean all other languages have to do the same...

While exploring encapsulation I also got to learn about the browser's local storage. So far I thought of data storage in terms of json files or other database languages but apparently the browser can help with data persistence too! While I had to reconfigure some stuff in my code for everything to be aligned with the use of the browser's local storage the extra functionality that was unlocked was worth the trouble.

Some interesting things I came across: Apparently arrow functions have a different scope than the traditionally typed ones, so if you use an arrow function inside an event listener anything referring to the this keyword inside the function won't be bound by the caller of the function, that is the event of the listener, but rather by the scope of the encapsulated app. Also apparently the constructor function part of classes serves more or less the same purpose as the whole constructor function approach methodology, so the prototype extension of each object/app is sort of more explicit in the constructor function approach.
